audit: No novel gene-diagnosis association survived scrutiny; every claim below is an established driver. Four of the strongest apparently novel signals are data artifacts, not biology: BCOR in Medulloblastoma, NOS (24 of 26 records), NOTCH2 in Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (19/19), NF2 in Pilocytic astrocytoma (13/13) and MED12 in Ependymoma, NOS (15 records, 7 impossible) carry protein positions far beyond the length of the protein (e.g. NOTCH2 p.E127469G, NF2 p.P21404E, BCOR p.K110637W) and/or missense changes that cannot arise from a single-nucleotide substitution (e.g. MED12 p.E1285C, p.A1285Y), whereas such records are ~0.05% of the rest of the file. They look injected or corrupted and were removed (MED12/ependymoma entirely, since the plausible-looking remainder is equally suspect); I would not report them and recommend auditing how the mutation table was assembled. Other concerns: 10 hypermutated cases (500-15,731 mutations, mostly malignant glioma; likely MMR/POLE) were excluded from testing; recurrent identical variants spread across unrelated diagnoses (C17orf80 p.S281R in 72 cases, HLTF p.Q898E, ZNF510 p.Q248E, CD69, CD46, SLAMF7, TSPAN19) suggest germline leakage or pipeline artifacts; BRAF V600E appears as p.V640E (alternate transcript); many diagnoses are vague or missing ('Neoplasm, NOS', 'missing', 'Unknown', 'Glioma, malignant') and overlapping labels split the same entity, diluting both cases and controls; most diagnoses have <15 cases so power is low; WES SNV/indel calls miss fusions and copy-number events (KIAA1549-BRAF, SMARCB1 deletions, RELA/YAP1 fusions, PAX-FOXO1), so expected frequencies are underestimates of true driver involvement. With ~93,000 gene-diagnosis tests, small-count 'novel' hits are expected by chance; I do not recommend headlining any as new findings.
methods: Gene-level binary mutation status per case (any non-synonymous call). Removed records with protein positions beyond the protein length (or >36,000) and missense changes not reachable by one nucleotide substitution; these were concentrated in four gene-diagnosis pairs and treated as artifacts. Excluded 10 hypermutated cases (>500 mutations). For each diagnosis label (n>=3) vs all other cases and each gene mutated in >=4 cases, a one-sided hypergeometric (Fisher) test; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across ~93k tests. Claims are FDR-significant pairs plus a few well-known drivers with nominal enrichment; probabilities combine FDR, effect size, sample size and prior biological knowledge; expected frequencies are lightly shrunken observed rates.
